title: Pakistan Period: Autonomy to Mass Uprising
tagline: Autonomy, representation, military rule, and the road to liberation
intro: Understand East Pakistan from the United Front and constitutional conflict to Six Points, Agartala, mass uprising, Bhola Cyclone, and the 1970 election.
description: Understand East Pakistan’s journey from language rights and constitutional conflict to autonomy demands, mass uprising, disaster politics, and the road to 1971.
seoTitle: Pakistan Period in East Bengal: Autonomy, Six Points, 1969 and the Road to 1971
seoDescription: Study East Pakistan through United Front, martial law, Six Points, Agartala Case, 1969 mass uprising, Bhola Cyclone, 1970 election, figures, and sources.
beginnerSummary: Start with the United Front, then follow military rule, autonomy demands, and mass politics that led toward the 1971 rupture.
advancedSummary: Compare constitutional imbalance, economic disparity, student movements, party strategies, disaster politics, and nationalist mobilization.

faq.question: Why is the Pakistan period central?
faq.answer: It shows how representation disputes, economic inequality, and language-cultural politics produced a mass autonomy movement.

faq.question: Why include the Bhola Cyclone?
faq.answer: The disaster and its political handling intensified distrust before the 1970 election and the 1971 crisis.

faq.question: Which sequence should I read?
faq.answer: Read United Front, martial law, Six Points, Agartala, 1969, and 1970 together as a chain of escalating autonomy politics.
